family.description: Members of this entry are serine/threonine-protein kinases and includes ATG1 from yeasts, Unc-51 from C. elegans and ULK1-2 from humans. ATG1 is required for vesicle formation in autophagy and the cytoplasm-to-vacuole targeting (Cvt) pathway [[cite:PUB00101056],[cite:PUB00066530]]. Unc-51 is important for axonal elongation and axonal guidance [[cite:PUB00042769]] and ULK1-2 are involved in autophagy in response to starvation [[cite:PUB00098424]]. They consist of a kinase domain at the N-terminal ([pfam:PF00069]) and two tandem microtubule interacting and transport (MIT) domains (tMIT) at the C-terminal. MIT domains are known to mediate protein-protein interactions. In ATG1, MIT domains mediate the interaction with ATG13 [[cite:PUB00101056]]. In ULK1-2, MIT domains control the regulatory function and localization of the proteins and also mediate interactions with additional autophagy proteins [[cite:PUB00098424]]. This is the C-terminal MIT domain (MIT2).
family.name: Atg1-like, MIT domain 1
